description: Given a 2D array triplets where each element is [a, b, c] and a target triplet [x, y, z], you can repeatedly pick two triplets and replace each value with the max of the two. Return true if the target can be obtained.
examples:
Input: triplets = [[2,5,3],[1,8,4],[1,7,5]], target = [2,7,5]
Output: true
Explanation: Take max of triplets[0] and triplets[2] to get [2,7,5].
intuition: A triplet is only useful if none of its values exceed the target - otherwise taking the max would overshoot. Among usable triplets, you just need to verify that each of the three target coordinates is achievable by at least one triplet.
approach: A triplet is usable if none of its values exceed the corresponding target value. Among usable triplets, check if we can match each target coordinate.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: triplets = [[2,5,3],[1,8,4],[1,7,5]], target = [2,7,5]
triplet [2,5,3]: 2<=2, 5<=7, 3<=5 -> usable
  t[0]=2==target[0]=2 -> good.add(0). good={0}
triplet [1,8,4]: 8 > 7 -> NOT usable, skip
triplet [1,7,5]: 1<=2, 7<=7, 5<=5 -> usable
  t[1]=7==target[1]=7 -> good.add(1)
  t[2]=5==target[2]=5 -> good.add(2). good={0,1,2}
good.size === 3 -> return true
explanation:
1. A triplet is "usable" only if all its values are <= the corresponding target values.
2. If any value exceeds target, taking max with it would overshoot.
3. Among usable triplets, check if each target coordinate is matched exactly.
4. If all 3 coordinates are covered by usable triplets, return True.
5. The max operation can combine multiple usable triplets.
hints: Skip any triplet where any value exceeds the corresponding target value.
Among remaining triplets, check if each target position can be exactly matched.
You only need to find one triplet per position that matches the target value.

phases.label: Check three coordinates for target matches

timeComplexityBreakdown.note: Triplets have exactly three values; the inner loop has fixed length.
